title: How Much Does an AI Agent Cost? Pricing Explained (2026)
summary: Ready-made AI agent plans run from free to $800 a month. I broke down every pricing model so you know what to budget before you commit.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** An AI agent costs $0 to $800 a month on the ready-made plans covered here, and the main paid plans sit at about $20 to $150. Building your own starts at about $5,000 for a simple agent built on a tool like Zapier and $25,000 for a basic custom one. For a set business role, I'd start with[Marblism](https://www.marblism.com/) , where one monthly price covers all 7 AI Employees with no charge per task or call. For a general assistant, I'd start with Claude Free, which costs nothing.


I've split the rest into 3 parts:


- **What you pay:** the 5 ways AI agents charge, AI receptionist plans, free plans and hidden costs.
- **Rent, build or hire:** what building your own costs and how a plan compares with paying a person.
- **Your own bill:** what Marblism's flat plan gets you and how it scores across 27 jobs, how to work out what you'd pay, and where I'd start.


How Much Does an AI Agent Cost? Pricing Explained (2026) Product How it charges Starting price What it includes


Marblism Flat rate per AI employee (one price for all 7 together) $24/mo on the yearly plan All 7 AI Employees, 50 hours of AI work a month, unlimited team members and businesses

ChatGPT Per seat $0 (Free) Unlimited text chats, with limits on uploads, images and deep research. Plus costs $20/mo


Gemini Per seat $0 (Free) Flash-Lite model, Deep Research, Gemini Live, 15 GB of storage. Google AI Pro costs $19.99/mo


Zapier Agents Per activity (each action it takes) $0 (Free) 400 activities a month


Lindy Per credit ($0.01 each) $49.99/mo per active user (Team) 5,000 credits a month


Fin by Intercom Per outcome (each problem it solves) $0.99 per outcome At least 50 a month on a helpdesk other than Intercom


Sintra Flat rate with credits $15.60/mo on the yearly plan 250 credits a month


Smith.ai Per call $0 (Free) 25 calls a month


My AI Front Desk A monthly bank of minutes $79/mo billed yearly ($99 monthly) 200 call minutes, 100 chatbot conversations, 400 texts


Goodcall Per caller, each counted once a month $79/mo (Starter) 100 callers a month, about 150 calls


All prices are from each company's own pricing page, captured between October 19 and November 12, 2026, and linked in each section.


## How much does an AI agent cost per month


An AI agent costs $0 to $800 a month on the plans shown here, and more on custom plans for large companies. An AI agent is software that does a job on its own, working out the steps toward the goal you give it and using its tools to finish them. The same word covers a general assistant that answers your questions, an automation tool that links actions across your apps, and a voice agent that picks up your calls. The price depends on how each company charges.


AI agents charge in 5 ways:


- **Per seat:** one fixed price a month for each person who uses it.
- **Per activity or credit:** a charge for every action the agent takes.
- **Per outcome:** a charge only when the agent solves a problem, such as a customer question it answers in full.
- **Flat rate per AI employee:** one monthly price for AI employees that each do a set job. On Marblism, one $24 monthly price covers all 7 together, not each one.
- **Per call or per minute:** for voice agents that answer your phone.


Which way of paying fits depends on where your work comes from.


Prices are a month, with the free plan first and the main paid plan second. Claude's and Marblism's are on yearly billing.


### Per seat: general AI assistants


With per-seat pricing, you pay one fixed price a month for each user, and you can use the agent as much as the plan's limits allow.[Claude](https://claude.com/pricing) ,[ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/pricing/) and[Gemini](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/) charge this way, and so does[Microsoft 365 Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/business) .

Gemini Google AI Ultra From $99.99/mo Highest access to Gemini 4 Argon, Chrome auto browse, from 20 TB of storage 5x AI Pro's usage, or 20x at $199.99/mo


Gemini Enterprise Business edition From $21 per user a month Ready-made Google agents, a Workflow Builder that needs no code, 25 GiB of shared storage per user Up to 300 users


Microsoft 365 Copilot Business Add-on to a Microsoft 365 plan From $18 per user a month, paid yearly (discounted from $21) Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, ready-made agents Some advanced AI features cost extra, based on use


All 3 start free, put the main paid plan at about $20 a month and the top plan from about $100.


Per-seat plans suit one person using one assistant for many kinds of work, because no task is counted. A heavy day can hit the limit, though, and on Claude Pro you then wait for the 5-hour limit to reset.


I'd pick it for a general assistant, because the bill is the same every month.


### Per activity or credit: automation agents


On[Zapier Agents](https://zapier.com/pricing) , an activity is any action the agent takes, such as:


- a step in a task, or a reply in chat
- visiting a web page
- looking something up in files you gave it


Each page visit and each search counts as an activity of its own, so one job with many steps uses many activities.


Per activity or credit: automation agents Product Plan Price What is included Extra cost or limit


Zapier Agents Free $0 400 activities a month Test runs count toward the 400. Up to 10 activities per job


Zapier Agents Pro $50/mo monthly or $33.33/mo billed yearly 1,500 activities a month Up to 40 activities per job, then the agent stops and waits for you


Lindy Team $49.99/mo per active user 5,000 credits a month at $0.01 each Extra credits cost $10 per 1,000. Unused monthly credits do not carry over


[Lindy](https://www.lindy.ai/pricing) charges each task in credits, at $0.01 a credit, and the number a task uses varies a lot:


Per activity or credit: automation agents Lindy task Credits Cost at $0.01 a credit


Everyday asks: answers, summaries, lookups, drafting a reply 2 to 250 $0.02 to $2.50


Deep work: researching a competitor, sorting a queue of support tickets 250 to 1,000 $2.50 to $10


Big builds 1,000 to 2,500 $10 to $25


Paying per use suits light work, because you pay only while the agent works. On Zapier Pro, 1,500 activities a month covers about 300 jobs of 5 activities each. On paid Zapier plans, test runs don't count toward the limit. When Lindy's credits run out, it stops the work that uses credits until next month, so there is no surprise bill.


A job with more steps uses up the monthly activities faster.


### Per outcome: pay only when the agent resolves


[Fin by Intercom](https://fin.ai/pricing) charges $0.99 per outcome. An outcome is usually a customer problem Fin solves, which means the customer asks for no more help after its last answer. Fin also charges when it finishes a set of steps you built that ends by passing the customer to a person or to another process.


Per outcome: pay only when the agent resolves Product Plan Price What is included Extra cost or limit


Fin by Intercom With a helpdesk other than Intercom $0.99 per outcome Solved problems, handovers to a person, leads turned away as a poor fit, leads sent to sign up on their own At least 50 outcomes a month


Fin by Intercom With the Intercom helpdesk $0.99 per outcome, plus $19 a month per helpdesk user The same outcomes The user fee on top


Fin for Sales Qualified leads $9.99 each A lead Fin checks and finds is a good fit Charged per qualified lead


Fin charges once per conversation, however many questions the customer asks or steps Fin runs. There is no charge when:


- the conversation goes to one of your team before Fin solves anything
- a set of steps Fin runs fails
- a customer asks for a person


Fin suits a business with a lot of support questions that Fin can answer on its own. You pay for at least 50 outcomes a month, which is $49.50, so it never starts at $0.


After that, the bill rises with each one. At 5 solved questions a day, about 150 a month, Fin costs about $148.50.


### Flat rate per AI employee: role-specific agents


A flat rate is one price a month that includes a set amount of work, counted in hours or credits, with no charge per action. I'd put[Marblism](https://www.marblism.com/pricing) , an[AI Employee](https://www.marblism.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-employee) platform, first here.


Flat rate per AI employee: role-specific agents Product Plan Price What is included Extra cost or limit


Marblism Yearly $24/mo All 7 AI Employees, 50 hours of AI work a month, unlimited team members, unlimited businesses Extra hours for sale at any time


Marblism Monthly $44/mo The same plan The same


Sintra Yearly $15.60/mo ($187.20 for 12 months) 250 credits a month Credits reset monthly. You can buy more when they run out


Sintra Monthly $48.50/mo (discounted from $97) 250 credits a month The same


Marblism counts that work in hours. Every plan includes 50 hours of AI work a month, and the hours reset each month. Only advanced AI actions use them, and chat and quick tasks don't. While the work fits in those hours, a busy month costs the same as a quiet one, whether Rachel answers 30 calls or 300.


[Sintra](https://sintra.ai/pricing) costs less than Marblism on the yearly plan, at $15.60 a month. On monthly billing it costs more, at $48.50 at its discounted price against Marblism's $44. Sintra's AI employees use up credits on chat messages and task replies, and Marblism's hours never count those.


I'd pick a flat rate if you want a set job, like answering the phone or posting on social media, done every day without counting tasks. If a big month uses up the included hours, you can buy more.


### Per call or per minute: AI voice agents


With per-call pricing, you pay for each call the agent answers.[Smith.ai](https://smith.ai/pricing/ai-receptionist) charges per call, so a long call costs the same as a short one. On its Pro plans, 150 calls a month cost $270.

Smith.ai AI Receptionist Pro $150/mo 75 calls ($2.00 a call) $2.50 per extra call


Smith.ai AI Receptionist Pro $270/mo 150 calls ($1.80 a call) $2.30 per extra call


Smith.ai AI Receptionist Enterprise $500/mo 300 calls ($1.67 a call) $2.17 per extra call


Smith.ai AI Receptionist Enterprise $800/mo 500 calls ($1.60 a call) $2.10 per extra call


My AI Front Desk Business-in-a-Box $99/mo, or $79/mo billed yearly 200 call minutes, 100 chatbot conversations, 400 texts, Zapier, alerts to 3 people 1,000 extra credits a month, and more added automatically when they run out


Goodcall Starter $79/mo 100 callers, about 150 calls 79 cents per extra caller


Goodcall Growth $129/mo 500 callers, about 750 calls 26 cents per extra caller


Goodcall Scale $299/mo 2,000 callers, about 3,000 calls 15 cents per extra caller


Every Smith.ai AI Receptionist plan includes:


- spam screening
- a dedicated phone number
- fluent English and Spanish
- 12+ voices
- FAQ answers that improve as it flags questions it could not answer
- no setup fees


[My AI Front Desk](https://www.myaifrontdesk.com/pricing) (Frontdesk AI) gives you a monthly bank of call minutes and is built for 1 to 10 calls, chats or texts a day.


[Goodcall](https://www.goodcall.com/pricing) counts each caller once a month, by phone number, however many times they call back. It charges nothing per minute, per call or for the AI's usage.


Each way of charging for calls suits a different business:


- Per call (Smith.ai) suits a steady number of calls, such as 75 a month on Pro for $150.
- A bank of minutes (My AI Front Desk) suits short, frequent calls.
- Per caller (Goodcall) keeps the bill steadiest when the same customers call back often.


### What that comes to per hour


To compare plans that charge in different ways, I worked out what each one costs per hour of work.


Marblism: $24 divided by the 50 included hours is $0.48 an hour on the yearly plan if you use them all, $0.88 on monthly billing. My AI Front Desk: $79 for 200 minutes is about $23.70 per hour of calls, about $29.70 on monthly billing. Smith.ai: $2.00 a call, at an assumed 4 minutes a call, is about $30 per hour of calls. What that comes to per hour Product Plan Unit Cost per unit Cost per hour of work


Marblism $24/mo yearly or $44 monthly Hour of AI work (50 included) $0.48 yearly, $0.88 monthly $0.48 yearly, $0.88 monthly


My AI Front Desk Business-in-a-Box, $79/mo billed yearly or $99 monthly Call minute (200 included) About $0.40 yearly, just under $0.50 monthly About $23.70 of calls yearly, about $29.70 monthly


Smith.ai AI Receptionist Pro, $150/mo Call (75 included) $2.00 About $30 of calls, if a call lasts 4 minutes


Zapier Agents Pro, $33.33/mo billed yearly or $50 monthly Job of 5 activities (300 jobs) About $0.11 yearly, about $0.17 monthly Billed per job


Lindy Team, $49.99/mo per active user Medium task of 250 credits (20 tasks) $2.50 Billed per task


Marblism costs the least per hour in the table, $0.48 on the yearly plan and $0.88 on monthly billing. The phone plans cost about $24 to $30 per hour of calls. One medium Lindy task costs $2.50.


An hour of Marblism's AI work and an hour of phone calls are different things. The column shows what each plan charges for its own kind of hour.


Zapier looks cheap per job until a job uses 20 activities. Then the same $50 covers only 75 jobs.


## How much does an AI receptionist cost


An AI receptionist for a small business starts at $0 a month. The price rises with the number of calls and depends on how each company charges. The cheapest paid plans for calls here cost $79 to $150 a month, and Smith.ai Enterprise starts at $500 a month. Rachel, Marblism's receptionist, comes in its flat plan with the other 6 AI Employees.


Main paid options, side by side:


How much does an AI receptionist cost Product Monthly price How it charges What's included


Marblism (Rachel) $24/mo on the yearly plan Flat rate Rachel plus the other 6 AI Employees, 50 hours of AI work


My AI Front Desk $99/mo (or $79/mo yearly) Bank of minutes 200 call minutes, 100 chatbot conversations, 400 texts


Smith.ai Pro $150/mo Per call 75 calls ($2.00/call)


Goodcall Starter $79/mo Per caller 100 callers a month (about 150 calls)


Goodcall Growth $129/mo Per caller 500 callers a month (about 750 calls)


Every plan above answers calls 24/7. In Marblism's[AI Employee Statistics 2026](https://www.marblism.com/research/ai-employee-statistics) report, 29% of the calls its AI receptionist answered came outside office hours (9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday, local time), and 1 in 9 at the weekend.


Day and night,[Rachel](https://www.marblism.com/ai-employees/rachel) :


- picks up every call
- schedules appointments directly into Google or Outlook calendars
- gets urgent calls through to your cell or office line right away
- switches to the caller's language, such as Spanish or French, and offers local numbers in the US, Canada, the UK, Mexico, and Australia


In the same report, Rachel dealt with 77% of calls without passing them on to the owner (June to September 2026). Separately, 1 in 10 callers she spoke to was spam. She is in every plan.


My AI Front Desk adds a built-in customer list (CRM), web chat and automatic follow-up messages to the call minutes. Smith.ai also checks whether a caller is a good lead, sends calls to the right person, records and transcribes calls, and introduces the caller before passing them on.


On Goodcall, a customer who calls back 5 times in a month counts as 1 caller. If your clients call often, the bill stays flat.


Here is how a per-call bill grows with more calls, next to the flat plan:


How much does an AI receptionist cost Calls a month Smith.ai bill (the plan that fits the calls) Marblism bill (yearly plan, Rachel included)


30 $15 (Free, 25 calls plus 5 extra at $3.00) $24


150 $270 (Pro, 150 calls) $24


300 $500 (300 calls) $24


If you are comparing phone tools, I keep a[separate guide to AI receptionists](https://www.marblism.com/blog/best-ai-receptionist) .


When you can't predict how many calls you'll get, how a plan charges matters more than the price on the page:


- On Smith.ai, each call is charged, so a busy month costs more.
- On Goodcall, a repeat caller counts once, so callers who ring back don't raise the bill.
- On My AI Front Desk, long calls can use up the minutes. The 1,000 extra credits a month cover about 40 more minutes, at 25 credits a minute.


## Is there a free AI agent?


Yes. Several products here have a free plan that does not run out after a set number of days.


What you get before you pay:


- **Claude Free** costs nothing and includes web search, file creation, running code, memory across conversations and links to your apps. Its usage limit resets every 5 hours. It is the widest free option here, and I'd start with it for everyday tasks before paying for anything else.
- **Zapier Agents Free** includes 400 activities a month at no cost. Test runs count toward the 400, and one job can use at most 10 activities. If your jobs take more than a few steps, the free plan runs out quickly.
- **Lindy** gives you $50 in credits with no card needed. They last 7 days, which makes it a trial. After that, paid use starts at $49.99 per user a month.
- **Smith.ai's AI Receptionist Free** plan covers 25 calls a month at no cost, with extra calls at $3.00 each.
- **My AI Front Desk** has no free plan, only a 7-day free trial. Paid plans start at $99 a month for Business-in-a-Box.
- With **Goodcall** , you can build the agent, test it and hear it answer before you pay anything. You start paying when you connect a phone number.


Every free plan here has a limit, on activities, credits, calls or how much you can use every few hours. They are a good way to test whether an AI agent can do one job for you. Past a few tasks or calls a day, a paid plan makes more sense.


## Hidden costs of running AI agents


Hidden costs are the limits and extra charges the price on the page doesn't show, such as actions counted one by one, credits that run out and monthly minimums.


Hidden costs of running AI agents Cost Product What happens


Extra activities Zapier Agents Each action and each page visit counts as an activity. A job stops at 10 activities on Free and 40 on paid plans


Credits used up fast Lindy A deep-work task uses 250 to 1,000 credits. Extra credits cost $10 per 1,000


Credits run out Lindy Unused monthly credits do not carry over. When they run out, work stops until next month, with no surprise bill


No charge per action Marblism Chat and quick tasks never use the 50 monthly hours. Extra hours for sale at any time


Monthly minimum Fin by Intercom You pay for at least 50 outcomes, $49.50 a month, on a helpdesk other than Intercom


Before you sign up, I'd check what each plan counts as something to charge for, so the first bill holds no surprise.


Extra credits you buy on Lindy stay until you use them, but the monthly ones do not carry over. On Zapier, a long job can hit the 40-activity limit and stop halfway until you step in, which costs you time.


## How much does it cost to build an AI agent


Building your own AI agent costs from about $5,000 for a simple one to $400,000 or more for a large company's system.[Appinventiv's 2026 cost guide](https://appinventiv.com/blog/ai-agent-development-cost/) puts the build at:


- $25,000 to $50,000 for a basic agent (one job, linked to one app)
- $50,000 to $150,000 for a mid-level agent
- $150,000 to $400,000 or more for a system built for a large company


[ProductCrafters' breakdown](https://productcrafters.io/blog/how-much-does-it-cost-to-build-an-ai-agent/) starts lower, at $5,000 to $15,000 for a simple agent built on Zapier or Make with little code. It puts the monthly cost of running one for a mid-sized company, with hosting, monitoring and tuning, at $2,000 to $10,000.


Appinventiv's and ProductCrafters' prices are for an agent that runs every day for real customers, with monitoring, fixes when something breaks, and upkeep. A rough test version you build yourself costs far less.


You also pay the AI model for each use. That bill is smaller than the build, but it comes every month.[Hivra's worked example](https://hivra.cloud/blog/ai-agent-api-cost-optimization) of an agent running 20 times a day puts it, at October 2026 rates, at:


- about $1 on Claude Haiku 5.5
- $22 on Sonnet 5.5
- $43 on Opus 5.5


An agent that visits a lot of websites, or several agents working together, costs more. Appinventiv puts the full monthly running cost (the AI model's usage, cloud hosting, monitoring and retraining) at $2,000 to $15,000 or more.


I worked out the build bars in the chart myself from the published ranges. The simple agent ("Low-code" in the chart) is ProductCrafters' lowest figure, $5,000, plus 12 months at $2,000 a month. Their monthly range is quoted for mid-sized companies, so that part is my assumption. Basic custom is the top of Appinventiv's basic range, $50,000, plus 12 months at $10,000 a month. Mid-level systems and systems for large companies cost more. Claude Pro is $200 a year up front or $20 a month. Marblism is $24 a month yearly or $44 monthly.


Running costs matter as much as the build. A rented plan starts at $0 with Claude Free, and Claude Pro gives at least 5x Free's usage every 5 hours. If you don't have a developer on staff, renting a plan for a set business role is faster and cheaper to start than a custom build in almost every case.


You can build one yourself, and Claude Max, which costs $100 a month, is one way to start building. If an AI employee plan already covers the job you need done, building is slower and riskier.


Marblism works the other way round and does not let you build your own agent. You hire from its 7 set roles, and in its own benchmark 7 of the 8 other products tested let you build one.


## Is an AI agent cheaper than hiring a person?


Yes, by a wide margin, for the 3 roles priced below: a receptionist, an executive assistant and a social media manager. At reception, a year of Marblism costs $288, a full-time virtual assistant (VA) about $31,200 and an employee about $54,300. For each role, a table shows the cost of an AI agent plan, a VA, and a full-time employee with salary plus benefits.


A VA still does better than an AI with:


- judgment calls
- messy one-off tasks
- anything that needs a person in the room or on the phone with a real human voice


### What a receptionist costs: AI agent vs virtual assistant vs employee


[Receptionists and information clerks earn a median of $18.27 an hour and $38,010 a year](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-4171.00) , according to 2025 data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).[BLS says benefits are about 30% of what private employers pay their staff](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm) , so a $38,010 salary comes to about $54,300 a year with benefits.


A virtual assistant covering reception work charges:


- [$10 to $20 an hour on Upwork](https://www.upwork.com/hire/virtual-assistants/cost/) (Upwork's published median range), or $20,800 to $41,600 a year full time
- [$7 to $13 an hour for an overseas freelancer doing customer support, in Wing Assistant's 2026 rate guide](https://wingassistant.com/blog/how-much-does-a-va-cost/) , or $14,560 to $27,040 a year
- $999 to $1,499 a month through an agency that manages the VA for you, like Wing, or $11,988 to $17,988 a year


At $15 an hour, the middle of Upwork's range, and 40 hours a week, a year of a VA at reception full time costs about $31,200. I compare every way of paying a VA in[what a virtual assistant costs](https://www.marblism.com/blog/virtual-assistant-cost) .


What a receptionist costs: AI agent vs virtual assistant vs employee AI agent plan Virtual assistant Full-time employee


Cost per month Marblism: $24 (yearly). My AI Front Desk: $79. Smith.ai Pro: $150. Goodcall: $79. About $2,600 full time at $15/hr About $4,525 with benefits


Cost per year Marblism: $288. My AI Front Desk: $948. Smith.ai: $1,800. Goodcall: $948. About $31,200 at $15/hr, 40 hrs a week About $54,300 with benefits (median salary $38,010)


Hours and availability 24/7, every day The hours you buy, typically business hours 40 hours a week, business hours, paid leave


Time to get started Minutes to set up Time to learn your business Time to hire, then time to train


What it cannot do Can't be there in person. Can't use its own judgment on an unusual caller. Not in your office. Hours depend on when they are free and their time zone. Business hours only. Holidays and sick days need cover. Weeks to hire and train.


Marblism's yearly plan, at $24 a month, is the AI plan. The VA rate is $15 an hour, the middle of Upwork's published $10 to $20 median range for virtual assistants, at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks. The employee cost is the BLS median receptionist wage of $38,010 with benefits at the same 30% share (BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation release, June 2026).


A VA covers the calls where a real voice matters. A hire covers the walk-ins.


### What an executive assistant costs: AI agent vs virtual assistant vs employee


[Executive secretaries and executive administrative assistants earn a median of $36.82 an hour and $76,590 a year](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-6011.00) , in the same 2025 BLS data. With benefits at the same 30% share, the total is about $109,400 a year.


An executive assistant VA charges:


- [$38 to $50 or more an hour on Upwork](https://www.upwork.com/hire/virtual-assistants/cost/) for experienced professionals
- [$10 to $18 an hour as an overseas freelancer in Wing Assistant's 2026 rate guide](https://wingassistant.com/blog/how-much-does-a-va-cost/)
- $1,299 to $1,999 a month through an agency


What an executive assistant costs: AI agent vs virtual assistant vs employee AI agent plan Virtual assistant Full-time employee


Cost per year Marblism (Eva): $288. Claude Pro: $200 to $240. ChatGPT Plus: $240. $15,588 to $23,988 through an agency About $109,400 with benefits (median salary $76,590)


Hours and availability 24/7, every day The hours you buy 40 hours a week, paid leave


What it cannot do Can't be in the room. Follows your rules and makes no judgment calls of its own. Not in your office. May not know your company's internal politics. One person for one role. Holidays, sick days, and turnover need a backup plan.


Eva clears your inbox and calendar. A VA or hire adds the in-person judgment and company context an AI cannot.


### What a social media manager costs: AI agent vs virtual assistant vs employee


For social media managers, the closest BLS job is public relations specialists, which includes social media work.[They earn a median of $35.94 an hour and $74,750 a year](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/27-3031.00) , in the same 2025 BLS data. With benefits, the total is about $106,800 a year.


A social media VA charges:


- [$8 to $15 an hour as an overseas freelancer in Wing Assistant's 2026 rate guide](https://wingassistant.com/blog/how-much-does-a-va-cost/)
- [$20 to $35 or more an hour on Upwork](https://www.upwork.com/hire/virtual-assistants/cost/) for marketing VAs, including social media marketing

## How to work out your own cost


3 choices set your cost:


- rent or build
- an agent for one role or a general assistant
- a flat price or paying per use


Before you pick a plan, count how many calls, tasks and support questions you handle a day. That number shows which way of paying keeps your bill steady.


Months in the chart have 30 days. A job is one Lindy task at 250 credits, one problem Fin solves (Fin charges for at least 50 a month), or one Smith.ai call on the cheapest plan for that number of calls. Marblism's line stays flat while the work fits its 50 included hours.

## FAQ


### Are AI agents worth it for a small business?


Yes, when a set role needs doing every day. Marblism's yearly plan costs about $288 a year, Rachel the receptionist included. A virtual assistant doing the same reception work costs about $31,200 a year at $15 an hour, the middle of Upwork's published range. If you only have a few tasks a week, start on a free plan. Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini all have one, and you can move to a paid plan once you outgrow its limit.


### Do AI agents charge per task?


Some do. Zapier Agents charges for each action, Lindy for the credits each task uses, and Fin $0.99 for each problem it solves. Claude and ChatGPT charge a fixed price per user, and Marblism one flat price, so the bill stays the same however many tasks you run within the plan's limits.


### What is the cheapest AI agent for a small business?


Free plans are the cheapest, such as Claude Free, Zapier Agents Free (400 activities a month) and Smith.ai's AI Receptionist Free (25 calls a month). Among the paid flat plans here, Sintra's yearly plan costs the least at $15.60 a month, though chat messages and task replies use up its credits. Marblism's yearly plan is $24 a month for all 7 AI Employees.


### How much does a ChatGPT agent cost?


[ChatGPT's pricing page](https://chatgpt.com/pricing) lists Free at $0, Go at $8, Plus at $20 and Pro from $100 a month. Dot, the agent that keeps working in the background, comes with Pro. For teams, a Business seat costs $20 a month per user billed yearly or $25 monthly, and Dots come with the Premium seat at $100 a month billed yearly or $125 monthly.


### How much does Marblism cost?


Marblism's yearly plan is $24 a month and the monthly plan is $44 a month. Both include all 7 AI Employees and 50 hours of AI work a month, and you can buy extra hours when those run out. A 7-day money-back guarantee covers the first payment.


### Does it cost money to run an AI agent?


Yes, on most setups. A ready-made plan costs its monthly fee to run, from $0 on a free plan. An agent you build yourself also pays the AI model for each use, every month. In Hivra's worked example, an agent running 20 times a day costs about $1 a month on Claude Haiku 5.5, $22 on Sonnet 5.5 and $43 on Opus 5.5 at October 2026 rates. Appinventiv puts the full running cost of a bigger system, including the AI model, cloud hosting, monitoring and retraining, at $2,000 to $15,000 or more a month.
